transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-22 15:00 PST
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Jules Park (Redwood AE), Mina Chopra (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood Solutions), Tom Hsu (Oakridge Head of ML), Priya Menon (Platform Eng), Carlos Ruiz (FinOps), Asha Patel (SRE)

Summary (auto): Console tour showing how Redwood surfaces usage by route and maps tokens to cost. Demonstrated per-route dashboards, tag-based filtering, and an example chargeback export. Discussed security (KMS, SSO), pilot steps, and benchmarking approach.

[00:00] Jules Park: ok everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run through a quick console demo focused on route level economics for inference — so usage, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. feel free to interrupt.
[00:18] Tom Hsu: yeah thanks, Jules. our ask is pretty focused: we have a few high-volume routes that look cheap on paper but surprise us at billing time. want to understand how we can map back to product teams and get predictable cost estimates.
[00:35] Jules Park: totally. that's exactly what the route dashboards are for. Mina will share the console and walk through a few examples.
[00:42] Mina Chopra: hi y'all opening the console now, bear with me while the sandbox loads. so first page is the usage lens — we show tokens, latency, and inferred cost over time. you can split by route which is a tag we recommend attaching at request time.
[01:05] Priya Menon: quick q — route tag, that's at SDK level or via reverse proxy? we put a bunch of metadata on the proxy layer.
[01:12] Mina Chopra: either works. SDK header or proxy header. we ingest route as a top-level attribute and it's indexed for dashboards and exports. sometimes it's called routeName, sometimes path. we've seen customers call it endpt, route, or product-team. console will normalize.
[01:31] Carlos Ruiz: how do you attribute multi-model flows? we have chains that hit a smaller reranker then a big generator — want to make sure chargeback is accurate.
[01:44] Mina Chopra: good point. we break down per-request by model call. so the dashboard shows stacked cost per-token by model call within a route. there is a per-model cost profile — you can pin different model/quant profiles. the transcript note: sometimes the auto transcriber messes up model names (e.g., "Aurora-7" might come out as "aura-7").
[02:05] Tom Hsu: ok. can you show an example where one route's latency SLO forced a more expensive model and drove cost up?
[02:14] Mina Chopra: sure. navigating to the 'Routes' view — here's Route: "Search-Snippet" — you can see volume on the left, cost on the right. on Jan 9 spike, SLA breach triggered routing policy to higher-tier model; cost per-call jumped from $0.012 to $0.045. in the console you can drill into policy decisions and the fallback history.
[02:40] Asha Patel: is that history exported? our finance folks want a CSV for chargeback.
[02:47] Mina Chopra: yes, export CSV including call-level rows and an aggregated per-route sheet. we also have an optimization export that highlights top N calls by cost.
[02:56] Liam O'Neal: just to add, the console supports sampling if you have high qps — we don't always export every token at call-level because of volume; we surface representative sampling with confidence intervals.
[03:09] Priya Menon: hmm sampling — can we control the sample rate per route? we have some critical routes we want full fidelity on.
[03:17] Mina Chopra: yep, per-route sampling overrides are available. you can pin full logging for up to X rps in the dedicated tier; for hosted we suggest a 1% baseline then bump for key routes.
[03:31] Tom Hsu: sweet. Carlos, any questions on the cost modeling?
[03:36] Carlos Ruiz: yeah two things — one, how does Redwood calculate per-token cost for quantized model variants, and two, do you include infra overhead like GPU amortization?
[03:48] Mina Chopra: for quantized models we use Redwood-verified throughput profiles. cost per-token is derived from measured throughput and the price for the model variant. infra overhead is surfaced in the dedicated pricing line if you're on Reserved/Dedicated; for hosted we present an all-in per-token cost but we also show a breakdown: model execution, batching overhead, infra surcharge, and egress if applicable.
[04:10] Tom Hsu: can you show the breakdown on a single call?
[04:15] Mina Chopra: yes — open a single call detail: there is timing and a cost waterfall: token decode cost, KV cache hit savings, batching efficiency, plus model variant multiplier. note: KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" in the raw — apologies.
[04:34] Priya Menon: what's KV cache hit rate look like for chatty routes? our chat bot calls are heavily prefix-based.
[04:43] Mina Chopra: you can see cache hit rate time series per route. for prefix-heavy chat it'll show higher hit rates and the console will project cost savings from enabling prefix/KV caching. we also recommend walleting old prompts to maximize cache reuse.
[05:00] Tom Hsu: walleting?
[05:03] Mina Chopra: sorry meant "caching patterns" — the transcriber likes unusual words.
[05:08] Carlos Ruiz: any hooks for FinOps? like mapping to chargeback tags or export to our finance system?
[05:15] Mina Chopra: yes, we support arbitrary tag mapping. you can map route -> product line -> cost center. exports include tag columns. plus we have a prepared chargeback template that plugs into NetSuite/Workday CSV ingestion.
[05:30] Tom Hsu: ok great. can you demo a hypothetical chargeback for three routes?
[05:35] Mina Chopra: walk through now. selecting three routes: Search-Snippet, Rewriter, and Topic-Classifier. toggle the time window to MTD. console computes total tokens, model time, and unit cost. then it applies user-defined rate (you can apply internal markups). here's an example where Search-Snippet is 62% of tokens but 78% of cost because it uses a larger generator on retries.
[06:05] Asha Patel: retries — do retries show as separate calls or aggregated?
[06:10] Mina Chopra: separate rows but we flag retries and you can collapse them. the retry reason is in the call metadata — e.g., timeout, low-confidence reroute, or manual fallback.
[06:22] Tom Hsu: fallback policies — how are these authored?
[06:26] Mina Chopra: policies are in the Control plane (we demo a UI) — simple rules: latency threshold -> fallback to cheaper model; cost threshold -> route to cached variant; tag-based overrides. they can also be API-driven by your sidecar.
[06:40] Liam O'Neal: quick note: for private deployments we can also expose audit logs to your SIEM. we support syslog and S3 archival.
[06:49] Priya Menon: that matters — SOC2, retention, and encryption at rest. what's the KMS story?
[06:56] Jules Park: we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated. for Hosted we have envelope encryption and can do customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. I'll follow up with the SOC2 pack and KMS notes.
[07:09] Tom Hsu: thanks. next, pilot. we want to run a 2-week pilot with representative traffic and measure cost delta and latency. what's the minimum set up?
[07:21] Mina Chopra: for a pilot we usually ask for: (1) list of 5 critical routes, (2) sample traffic export or production mirroring access, (3) sandbox tenant or dedicated pilot capacity, (4) SSO and infra contacts for VPC if private. we provide a pilot runbook and a measurement spreadsheet.
[07:40] Tom Hsu: sample traffic — is that redaction safe? we need to avoid PHI.
[07:46] Mina Chopra: yes we support schema-based redaction client-side or you can send sanitized samples. for the benchmark we only need payload sizes and typical prompt shapes; exact user data is not required.
[07:58] Carlos Ruiz: on pricing during pilot, do we get discounted pilot pricing?
[08:02] Jules Park: pilots are generally complimentary up to a threshold; beyond that we propose a short-term discounted rate. we'll include that in the pilot proposal.
[08:12] Priya Menon: one more technical: how real-time is the console? our ops need near real-time alerts if cost spikes.
[08:20] Mina Chopra: the console ingest is near real-time — dashboards update within 20-40s for hosted and slightly more for private depending on telemetry batching. there are alerting policies with webhooks and Slack integrations.
[08:33] Tom Hsu: good. any limitations on route cardinality? we have thousands of endpoints.
[08:40] Mina Chopra: console handles high cardinality; there are practical UI limits so we recommend grouping via naming conventions or tagging. backend supports millions of distinct tags but you should plan for sane aggregation.
[08:55] Asha Patel: can we do per-route sample traces to debug latency regressions?
[09:02] Mina Chopra: yes trace sampling with request-level timelines, kernel-level timing is available in Dedicated. for hosted we show end-to-end timing and model-stage timings.
[09:15] Tom Hsu: ok, I'm going to summarise the next steps on our side: we'll pick five routes and send sample shapes, and provide sandbox VPC details. Jules, you'll send SOC2 and pricing. Mina will push a sample CSV.
[09:28] Jules Park: yes that matches our action items. I can send an initial pilot proposal tomorrow.
[09:34] Priya Menon: quick security Q — SSO. can we enforce SAML groups -> console role mapping?
[09:40] Liam O'Neal: yes role mapping via SAML SCIM provisioning, and RBAC in console; we can demo mapping in a separate short session with your identity team.
[09:52] Tom Hsu: perfect. any mentions of other vendors?
[09:55] Carlos Ruiz: we did a POC with Anthropic's managed endpoints earlier; they lacked detailed per-route cost mapping. also evaluating Vertex's cost reports but it's noisy.
[10:08] Mina Chopra: ok noted.
[10:10] Jules Park: last admin note — I'll put tentative pilot week of Jan 11-22, subject to your infra availability.
[10:18] Tom Hsu: that works, we'll confirm by Jan 5. thanks everyone.
[10:22] [meeting end - informal wrap up]
